text:
mira: quick check — onboarding Mistral-X-7B. CI is failing on config validation for model bundle. Error says unknown field 'tokenizer_overrides'. anyone seen this?

sam: got the CI logs? did the schema bump to v3 land on main recently? :thinking_face:

mira: paste of failing output:
```
ERROR: config.json: validation failed
 - unknown field 'tokenizer_overrides' (allowed: model_name, weights_path, max_seq_len, default_tokens, quantization)
```

devon: yeah we merged schema v3 last week. We removed tokenizer_overrides in favor of a nested `default_tokens` object. Old bundles still using overrides will fail.

mira: ah. where are the weights / bundle source for this one? I only have a path in the onboarding ticket: s3://redwood-models/mistral-x/v1/ — is that canonical?

sam: correct path is s3://redwood-models/registered/mistral-x/2026-02-28/weights.tar.gz (the team started moving to registered/). The bundle in the ticket points to a temp upload.

riyah: tokenizer question: Mistral-X tokenizer sets BOS=1 EOS=2 PAD=0 but upstream repo has eos=50256 for the GPT mapping — we need to ensure our tokenizer shard has the right special ids or runtime will misalign kv-cache offsets.

mira: nice catch. The config in the bundle has:
```json
{
  "model_name": "mistral-x-7b",
  "weights_path": "s3://redwood-models/registered/mistral-x/2026-02-28/weights.tar.gz",
  "tokenizer_overrides": {
    "eos_token_id": 2
  },
  "max_seq_len": 2048
}
```

devon: convert to schema v3 by moving tokenizer_overrides -> default_tokens and add explicit pad/bos/eos. e.g.
```json
{
  "model_name": "mistral-x-7b",
  "weights_path": "s3://redwood-models/registered/mistral-x/2026-02-28/weights.tar.gz",
  "default_tokens": { "bos_id": "1", "eos_id": "2", "pad_id": "0" },
  "max_seq_len": 2048
}
```

sam: also ensure tokens are numbers (not strings) in the actual file; validator is strict. And add `kv_cache_compat: "v2"` when the bundle was generated with the kv-cache layout v2. Missing that will break warm-start.

mira: ok. quick Q: is there a helper script to do this migration? or should I update the bundle manually?

config-bot: Reminder: run `./tools/config-validator validate <bundle_dir>` before pushing to s3. See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/configs#v3 

devon: we added a migration helper at tools/migrations/tokenizer_to_default_tokens.py — call it with the extracted bundle dir and it will update config.json plus run basic checks. Example:
```bash
python tools/migrations/tokenizer_to_default_tokens.py --path /tmp/mistral-x-bundle
./tools/config-validator validate /tmp/mistral-x-bundle
```

mira: awesome — will run that. One more: CI was also complaining about missing `quantization` field when deploying to dedicated. What's the safe default?

sam: allowed values: none, int8, int4. For onboarding use `quantization: none` if you don't have a quantized artifact. Dedicated auto-fallback will pick a compatible variant if available.

riyah: note on tokenizer quirks — the vocab has a merged unk token; if `pad_id` == `unk_id` we should explicitly add `ignore_pad_tokens: true` in config to avoid doing pad gradient ops. This is a corner case we hit in evals.

mira: good call. I'll add defaults: `quantization: none`, `default_tokens` with bos/eos/pad as ints, and `kv_cache_compat: "v2"`. I'll run migration + validator and post CI link.

devon: ping me when CI is green, I'll approve the PR. :thumbsup:

mira: thanks — will update the onboarding ticket with final S3 path and new config snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/489 (WIP)

sam: :eyes: add the validator run command to the PR description so infra can replay locally.

mira: will do. tagging this as actioned for now.
